anchors: Given only a SID, run `snort why <ip>` for the GID before writing the fix.
decision: Identify a Snort rule to suppress as GID:SID; a bare SID means gen_id 1, and without an alert the GID is unknown and is not guessed.

evidence.text: A real pfSense 2.8.1 alert (125,9 ftp_telnet) was mapped to 'suppress gen_id 1, sig_id 9' by the previous tool output. RED on the pre-edit text: a haiku probe wrote gen_id 1 for that alert; GREEN on the edited text: opus and haiku used --sid 125:9 and quoted the governing sentence.

reopen_if: Snort or pfSense starts identifying rules by SID alone, or the tool stops accepting a bare SID.
why: A SID names a rule only together with its generator. A preprocessor alert (GID 125, SID 9) suppressed as gen_id 1, sig_id 9 suppresses a different rule, so the block recurs while the fix looks applied.

anchors: counts a scoped one only for the addresses you name with `--ip <blocked address>` (repeatable) or `--cidr`; without them it answers NO
An `ip` holding a variable or a `!` negation is not evaluated and also reads NO.
decision: A suppress line with track by_src or by_dst and ip counts only for the addresses its ip names; snort verify reports each line's scope, says yes for a scoped line only for addresses given with --ip or --cidr, and reads a variable or negation in ip as NO. fixsteps with --cidr offers the scoped form as a by_src and by_dst pair.

evidence.text: RED: test_snort_verify_without_an_address_does_not_call_a_scoped_suppression_complete failed on the unchanged code (verify exit 0 for a by_src-scoped line); pre-edit SKILL.md held no mention of track, by_src, by_dst or scope. GREEN: 19 new or changed tests pass, a 4-arm mutation battery is fully killed. Scope semantics: Snort README.filters (snort.org/faq/readme-filters); bracketed lists only from Snort mailing-list replies, not the manual.

reopen_if: Snort's own parser is shown to treat a scoped suppress differently (for example track by_src applying to both sides), or a pfSense release writes the suppress file in another shape, or verify gains a way to evaluate Snort variables.
why: verify counted 'suppress gen_id G, sig_id S, track by_src, ip X' as suppressing the rule for every address, so it said yes while every other source was still blocked. The scope semantics come from Snort's README.filters (snort.org/faq/readme-filters): the plain form suppresses the event completely, track by_src|by_dst with ip restricts it to that side of the alert, and ip takes a single address or a CIDR block. Bracketed lists are read member by member; variables and negations are not evaluated, so NO is the safe reading. Both sides are printed by fixsteps because the range can be the alert's source or destination depending on the rule.

anchors: keeps a freed dynamic entry there until dhcpd restarts
A reservation's DNS name moves only when unbound is rewritten.
decision: A reservation's DNS name (regdhcpstatic) moves only when services_unbound_configure() rewrites host_entries.conf; dhcp add and dhcp rm with --apply run it when the option is on, then restart unbound and check it answers, while dhcp rename leaves it to the reader. A freed dynamic lease (regdhcp) stays in dhcpleases_entries.conf until dhcpd restarts, so the reader checks that file and restarts the DHCP service if the old address is still there.

evidence.text: Field report from a pfSense box (2026-11-16) queued as a contribution; not re-run here. The script behaviour is pinned by the dhcp add/rm unbound tests in tests/test_pfsense.py.

reopen_if: pfSense rewrites the static-mapping and dynamic-lease name files on every DHCP reconfigure, or dhcp rename gains the same unbound step.
why: After a reservation was removed and re-added, unbound kept answering the reservation's name with the old address until services_unbound_configure() plus a restart, and a freed dynamic address stayed in dhcpleases_entries.conf until dhcpd restarted; nothing reported either, so the stale name went unnoticed.

anchors: keeps a freed dynamic entry there until dhcpd restarts
A reservation's DNS name moves only when unbound is rewritten.
decision: A reservation's DNS name (regdhcpstatic) moves only when services_unbound_configure() rewrites host_entries.conf; dhcp add, dhcp rename and dhcp rm with --apply run it when the option is on, then restart unbound and check it answers. A freed dynamic lease (regdhcp) stays in dhcpleases_entries.conf until dhcpd restarts, so the reader checks that file and restarts the DHCP service if the old address is still there.

evidence.text: Field report from a pfSense box (2026-11-16) queued as a contribution; not re-run here. The script behaviour for add, rename and rm is pinned by the dhcp unbound tests in tests/test_pfsense.py.

reopen_if: pfSense rewrites the static-mapping and dynamic-lease name files on every DHCP reconfigure.
why: A rename changes the very name unbound registers, so leaving it out of the reconfigure kept the old name answering exactly as a removal without the reconfigure did; the three DHCP writes now share one unbound step instead of the text sending rename readers to do it by hand.

anchors: refused unless git ignores that folder and nothing in it is tracked
decision: A snapshot directory inside a git work tree is accepted without --allow-repo-snapshot when git check-ignore (index mode, never --no-index) names the directory itself, which it does not for a folder holding a tracked file; any other folder in a work tree is refused unless --allow-repo-snapshot is passed. The skill also says an existing folder keeps its mode and only draws a readable-by-others warning, which chmod cannot clear on an SMB/CIFS mount.

evidence.text: Scratch-repo probes: check-ignore of configs/ (ignored, nothing tracked) answers rc 0 and echoes the path; of a folder with a force-added file answers rc 1 in index mode and rc 0 with --no-index. Tests in tests/test_pfsense.py pin ignored, new-below-ignored, unignored, tracked (two depths), git error and empty-answer cases, and an end-to-end --apply.

reopen_if: git check-ignore stops reporting a directory with tracked contents as not ignored, or a site needs snapshots in a tracked folder.
why: A site's dated config copies usually live in a gitignored folder of its own machine repo, and the old refusal made every change there need --allow-repo-snapshot, which also lifts the guard for folders git would stage. Asking git about the directory keeps the protection for tracked and unignored folders while letting the common site layout through.

anchors: an empty value kills nothing on an alarm, so a box where it is empty needs no change for this
decision: Name gw_down_kill_states=all as the cause of every-connection drops on a saturated line; on a single WAN set it to none and tick Disable Gateway Monitoring Action; an empty value kills nothing on an alarm in 2.8.1, so read the value before carrying the fix to another box.

evidence.text: filter.inc and gwlb.inc read on a 2.8.1 box: only all reaches pfctl -Fs, down kills by gateway, action_disable drops -C rc.gateway_alarm from dpinger; three saturated-line test loads each logged a flush-all line, none after the change.

reopen_if: A pfSense release changes the state-kill loop in filter.inc (the empty or none handling, or the action_disable skip).
why: A saturated line raises dpinger alarms, and with Flush all each alarm runs pfctl -Fs plus a filter and VPN reload; a box where the value is empty needs no change, so copying the fix blindly changes a setting that is already right.

anchors: Arm a dead-man guard ON the firewall first; it restores the old config unless you confirm in time
decision: Before a gateway or routing change on a box with no console and no hypervisor snapshot, arm an on-box dead-man guard that restores config.xml unless confirmed; run the edit detached; confirm by touching the ok file first, then killing the guard's sleep.

evidence.text: Shell semantics simulated: ok file then kill sleep, the sh exits with no rollback; kill sleep without the file, rollback runs; kill sh, the sleep stays with parent 1. daemon usage on 2.8.1 confirms -p is the child pidfile. The rollback branch itself never fired on a box.

reopen_if: The rollback branch is exercised on a live box and rc.reload_all does not restore the old routing, or pfSense gains a built-in confirm-or-revert for config changes.
why: A broken default route takes the only remote path in with it, and config.xml is then the only rollback; killing the guard's sh instead of its sleep orphans the sleep, and killing the sleep before the ok file exists fires the rollback.

anchors: and the dpinger processes it started were gone once the session ended
decision: Start daemons from an ssh session detached (daemon -f -o <log> ...) and check them with pgrep -x on the box.

evidence.text: One observed incident on a 2.8.1 box, reported by its operator; the mechanism is not established (gwlb.inc sends dpinger stdout and stderr to /dev/null).

reopen_if: A detached start is shown to lose daemons too, or the hang is traced to a cause a plain ssh call avoids.
why: A playback that ran setup_gateways_monitor() over ssh hung until the timeout and the dpinger processes it started were gone after the session ended, leaving no gateway monitoring.

anchors: set the shaper below the measured rate and lower it until loaded ping stays near idle
decision: Measure the real line rate and loaded latency from the firewall (and a LAN host) before choosing any shaper rate; shape only when loaded ping rises, below the measured rate, lowering until loaded ping stays near idle.

evidence.text: One line sold at about 25 Mbit measured 22.1/21.4 with ping 11 ms idle and 39 ms loaded under shapers at 23/24, idle-level ping at 21/20; another measured 408/54 with 7 ms idle and loaded.

reopen_if: A shaper set above the measured rate is shown to keep loaded latency at idle.
why: A shaper at or above the real rate never fills, so the queue forms at the provider and firewall-side fairness does nothing; a line whose loaded ping does not rise gains nothing from a shaper.

anchors: ignores the limiter's mask, so a host with eight connections gets eight shares
decision: State that dummynet FQ-CoDel is fair per connection and ignores masks, a pipe mask gives a per-host cap, and a per-host share needs WF2Q+ with a masked child queue whose CoDel parameters are written explicitly.

evidence.text: fq_codel_classify_flow in FreeBSD dn_sched_fq_codel.c hashes the packet 5-tuple with no mask; shaper.inc on 2.8.1 takes codel target and interval defaults from net.inet.ip.dummynet.codel sysctls; filter.inc emits dnqueue for a child queue; A/B figures from one line.

reopen_if: FreeBSD's fq_codel classifier starts honouring the scheduler mask.
why: Readers reach for an FQ-CoDel limiter with a mask to share a line per host and get either per-flow fairness or per-host caps.

decision: Do not prescribe a fixed fraction of the measured rate (such as 85-90%) for a shaper.

evidence.text: Measured 22.1/21.4 Mbit; shapers at 21/20 kept ping at idle values, 20/19 against 21/20 showed the same ping.

reopen_if: Measurements on several lines show a stable fraction below which loaded ping stays at idle and above which it does not.
why: The measured line kept idle-level ping with a shaper at about 93-95% of its measured rate, so a fixed 85-90% rule is not supported by the evidence and costs throughput; the skill gives a procedure (lower until loaded ping stays near idle) instead.
